arxiv-2011-07828.title: Ruin Probabilities with Investments: Smoothness, IDE and ODE, Asymptotic Behavior
arxiv-2011-07828.creator: Yuri KABANOV, Nikita PUKHLYAKOV
arxiv-2011-07828.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yuri KABANOV, Nikita PUKHLYAKOV. The study deals with the ruin problem when an insurance company having two business branches, life insurance and non-life insurance, invests its reserve into a risky asset with the price dynamics given by a geometric Brownian motion. We prove a result on smoothness of the ruin probability as a function of the initial capital and obtain for it an integro-differential equation understood in the classical sense.

arxiv-2108-12854.title: Keller-type bounds for Dirac operators perturbed by rigid potentials
arxiv-2108-12854.creator: Haruya Mizutani and Nico M. Schiavone
arxiv-2108-12854.description: Abstract In this paper we are interested in generalizing Keller-type eigenvalue estimates for the non-selfadjoint Schrödinger operator to the Dirac operator, imposing some suitable rigidity conditions on the matricial structure of the potential, without necessarily requiring the smallness of its norm.

arxiv-2203-06136.title: A trace inequality of Ando, Hiai and Okubo and a monotonicity property of the Golden-Thompson inequality
arxiv-2203-06136.creator: Eric A. Carlen, Elliott H. Lieb 1 . 1. Department of Mathematics, Hill Center,[-6pt] Rutgers University, 110 Frelinghuysen Road Piscataway NJ 08854-8019 USA 2 . 2. Departments of Mathematics and Physics, Jadwin Hall,[-6pt] Princeton University, Princeton, NJ 08544
arxiv-2203-06136.description: Abstract The Golden-Thompson trace inequality which states that T ​ r ​ e H + K ≤ T ​ r ​ e H ​ e K Tr\,e^{H+K}\leq Tr\,e^{H}e^{K} has proved to be very useful in quantum statistical mechanics. Golden used it to show that the classical free energy is less than the quantum one.

arxiv-2207-03041.title: Vision Transformers: State of the Art and Research Challenges
arxiv-2207-03041.creator: Bo-Kai Ruan, Hong-Han Shuai, Wen-Huang Cheng
arxiv-2207-03041.description: Abstract Transformers have achieved great success in natural language processing. Due to the powerful capability of self-attention mechanism in transformers, researchers develop the vision transformers for a variety of computer vision tasks, such as image recognition, object detection, image segmentation, pose estimation, and 3D reconstruction.

arxiv-2302-06576.title: GFlowNet-EM for Learning Compositional Latent Variable Models
arxiv-2302-06576.creator: Edward J. Hu, Nikolay Malkin, Moksh Jain, Katie Everett, Alexandros Graikos, Yoshua Bengio
arxiv-2302-06576.description: Abstract Latent variable models (LVMs) with discrete compositional latents are an important but challenging setting due to a combinatorially large number of possible configurations of the latents. A key tradeoff in modeling the posteriors over latents is between expressivity and tractable optimization. For algorithms based on expectation-maximization (EM), the E-step is often intractable without restrictive approximations to the posterior.

arxiv-2511-07898.title: A Novel Block-Alternating Iterative Algorithm for Retrieving Top- k k Elements from Factorized Tensors
arxiv-2511-07898.creator: Chuanfu Xiao, Jiaxin Zeng*, Ji Q. Ren & Yevgeny LeNet, Coauthor
arxiv-2511-07898.description: Abstract Tensors, especially higher-order tensors, are typically represented in low-rank formats to preserve the main information of the high-dimensional data while saving memory space. In practice, only a small fraction elements in high-dimensional data are of interest, such as the k k largest or smallest elements.

pmc-12526646.title: LCW-YOLO: A Lightweight Multi-Scale Object Detection Method Based on YOLOv11 and Its Performance Evaluation in Complex Natural Scenes
pmc-12526646.creator: Gang Li, Juelong Fang
pmc-12526646.description: Accurate object detection is fundamental to computer vision, yet detecting small targets in complex backgrounds remains challenging due to feature loss and limited model efficiency. To address this, we propose LCW-YOLO, a lightweight detection framework that integrates three innovations: Wavelet Pooling, a CGBlock-enhanced C3K2 structure, and an improved LDHead detection head.

pmc-13029872.creator: Andrew Capalbo, Francis Letendre, Alexander Langner, Abigail Blackburn, Owen Dillahay, Michael Twardowski
pmc-13029872.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Four CNN-based classification algorithms were successfully implemented for categorizing zooplankton with >95% accuracy using over 70k images.Niched networks are a tractable, modular and efficient avenue for specific taxonomic or functional classification. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13353788.title: The gut microbiome and mitochondrial function in metabolism, immunity, and disease
pmc-13353788.creator: Eui Jeong Han, Da-Hye Kim, Jeong Jae Lee, Hea-Jong Chung
pmc-13353788.description: The gut microbiome is a key regulator of host physiology, yet its effects remain difficult to predict across individuals and contexts. Similar microbial compositions frequently give rise to divergent and delayed phenotypic outcomes, indicating that models based solely on signal strength or steady-state responses are insufficient to explain microbiome-driven host function.

pmc-13584140.title: The critical role of 16S rRNA sequencing in diagnosis and management of an odontogenic deep neck abscess: A case report
pmc-13584140.creator: Annachiara Ghiotti, Jacopo Monticelli, Marina Busetti, Michele Maglione, Stefano Di Bella, Fabio Barbone, Raffaella Koncan
pmc-13584140.description: Odontogenic abscesses are characteristically polymicrobial infections where fastidious anaerobes play a critical role. Conventional culture methods often fail to identify these pathogens, leading to diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We present a case of a severe deep neck and metastatic lung abscess following third molar extraction.
